short: A smooth metric with no local immersion in $\mathbb{R}^3$

title.title: A smooth surface metric that no piece of $\mathbb{R}^3$ realizes
title.subtitle: Claim: a $C^\infty$ metric on $(-1,1)^2$ with no smooth isometric immersion of any neighbourhood of 0 into $\mathbb{R}^3$

plain: A smooth rule for distances on a tiny patch that no piece of ordinary 3D surface can follow

object.heading: Schematically: sign-changing curvature patches, shrinking to the origin

beats.text: Analytic metrics always embed locally (Janet–Cartan). Smooth ones were open
On each patch, a would-be height function must solve the Darboux equation
A boundary-saddle argument rules it out on one patch, so no immersion exists

steps: Glue infinitely many shrinking patches where the curvature flips sign
Any immersion would give a height function solving one equation
On one patch a saddle argument says it can't: no immersion

achievement.label: Local isometric embedding of smooth surface metrics
achievement.context: Before: Pogorelov's $C^{2,1}$ metric with no $C^2$ realization; smooth ones open
achievement.note: Uses both signs of curvature: the $K \ge 0$ and $K \le 0$ cases stay open

verify.detail: Main theorem in Lean: about 57,500 lines under OAI/Geometry/IsometricImmersion
verify.ourCheck: We read the Comparator statement; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Analytic rules always fit near a point. For smooth ones, it was open.
Shrinking patches flip curvature; on one, a saddle argument breaks any fit.
Claimed: no neighbourhood fits in three dimensions.

sources.quote: There is a C-infinity positive-definite metric g on (-1,1)^2, agreeing with the Euclidean metric to infinite order at the origin, such that no neighbourhood of the origin admits a C-infinity isometric immersion into R^3.
Pogorelov: C^{2,1} metric with no C^2 realization

The paper glues infinitely many shrinking patches where the curvature changes sign and shows any immersion would give a height function obeying the Darboux equation that a boundary-saddle argument rules out on one of the patches.

sources.quote: In Lean (`OAI/Geometry/IsometricImmersion`, about 57,500 lines). The metric needs both curvature signs, so the $K \ge 0$ and $K \le 0$ versions remain open.
